rules.statement: Store public key material (such as SubjectPublicKeyInfo or a public-only certificate) unprotected; do not wrap it with a data protector the way private keys are wrapped.
rules.why: A public key is not confidential. Protecting it adds cost and key-management coupling with no security benefit, and it hides the fact that the material is public.
rules.check: Look for public-only key material (SPKI bytes, public JWK parameters, certificates without a private key) being passed through IDataProtector.Protect or a similar wrapper before it is stored.

rules.statement: Model a verify-only (public-only) asymmetric key as a subclass of the existing RSA/ECC key abstraction, not as a separate parallel type, so that code resolving keys by the base type and the signature algorithms keep working unchanged.
rules.why: A parallel hierarchy would split key resolution apart. Subclassing lets every consumer that resolves by the RSA/ECC base type, and every verify path, work without changes.
rules.check: Look for a new public-key or verify-only key type that does not derive from the existing algorithm-specific key base class, or for key resolution code that adds separate branches for public-only keys.

rules.statement: When building a key from an X509Certificate2 that has no private key, produce a verify-only key from the certificate's public key instead of throwing.
rules.why: Relying parties register only their public certificates or keys. Rejecting public-only material makes verification flows such as private_key_jwt and JAR impossible.
rules.check: Look for key-creation code that checks HasPrivateKey and throws ArgumentException (or similar) where a public-only certificate should give a verification key.
